translations.literal: Day yiwei: envoys were sent to comfort eastern Jing flood victims.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei eastern Jing flood victims received commissioners.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以張士遜為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Day dingyou: Zhang Shirun was made deputy military affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou Zhang Shirun became deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 己亥，宴近臣承明殿。

translations.literal: Day jihai: close ministers were feasted at the Hall of Accepting Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai intimates dined at Accepting Brightness.

sentences.zh: 二月甲寅，審刑院言天下無斷獄。

translations.literal: Second month, day jiayin: the Court for Reviewing Punishments reported that the realm had no cases awaiting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, jiayin: the review court reported zero pending cases nationwide.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，賜天下酺。

translations.literal: Day bingyin: a feast was granted throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the empire was given a public holiday feast.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以孔子四十七世孫聖祐襲封文宣公。

translations.literal: Day gengwu: Confucius’s forty-seventh-generation descendant Shengyou was enfeoffed as Duke of Literary Propagation.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Kong Shengyou, Confucius’s forty-seventh heir, became Duke of Literary Propagation.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，禦正陽門觀酺。

translations.literal: Third month, day xinsi: he viewed the feast at the Gate of Correct Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Third month, xinsi: he watched revels at the Gate of Correct Yang.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，京東、西水災，賜民租十之五。

translations.literal: Day xinchou: eastern and western Jing flood victims were granted five-tenths remission of rent.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou flood districts in eastern and western Jing got half their rent forgiven.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，丁謂加司空，馮拯加左僕射，曹利用加右僕射，任中正工部尚書。

translations.literal: Day renyin: Ding Wei was made Minister of Works; Feng Zheng was made Left Vice Director; Cao Liyong was made Right Vice Director; Ren Zhongzheng was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Ding Wei took Works; Feng Zheng the left; Cao Liyong the right; Ren Zhongzheng Works as well.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙辰，客星出軒轅。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day bingchen: a guest star appeared at the Chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, bingchen: a guest star blazed in the Chariot constellation.

sentences.zh: 五月乙亥，慮囚，降天下死罪。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day yihai: prisoners were reviewed; capital crimes throughout the realm were reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, yihai: a prison review commuted death sentences empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 六月丙午，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day bingwu: Venus appeared in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month, bingwu: Venus shone at noon.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲戌朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, day jiaxu new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month, jiaxu new moon: the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，新作景靈宮萬壽殿。

translations.literal: Day wuyin: the new Longevity Hall of the Hall of Numinous Splendor was completed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Longevity Hall at the Hall of Numinous Splendor was finished.

sentences.zh: 八月壬戌。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day renxu.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month, renxu.

sentences.zh: 熒惑犯南斗。

translations.literal: Mars entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: Mars crossed the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 九月戊寅，唃廝囉請降。

translations.literal: Ninth month, day wuyin: Gusiluo requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month, wuyin: Gusiluo offered to submit.

sentences.zh: 冬十月癸卯，蠲京東西、淮、浙被災民租。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day guimao: rent was remitted for the people of eastern and western Jing, Huai, and Zhe struck by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, guimao: disaster rent was cut in eastern and western Jing, Huai, and Zhe.

sentences.zh: 壬子，依漢、唐故事，五日一受朝，遇慶會，皇太子押班。

translations.literal: Day renzi: following Han and Tang precedent, audience would be held every five days; on festive occasions the crown prince would lead the line.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Han-Tang custom returned—audience every five days, the crown prince leading on feast days.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊子，王欽若以山南東道節度使坐擅赴闕，降司農卿、分司南京。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day wuzi: Wang Qinruo, military commissioner of Shannan East, was demoted for coming to court without leave to Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries, assigned to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, wuzi: Wang Qinruo was punished for rushing to court unbidden—demoted to granary director at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高麗遣使來貢。

translations.literal: That year Goryeo sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year Goryeo sent tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 京東、河北、兩川、荊湖稔。

translations.literal: Eastern Jing, Hebei, the Two Sichuans, and Jing-Hu had good harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jing, Hebei, both Sichuans, and Jing-Hu ripened well.

sentences.zh: 乾興元年春正月辛未朔，改元。

translations.literal: First year of Qianxing, spring, first month, day xinwei new moon: the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxing year one, spring, xinwei new moon: the reign title changed.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，禦東華門觀燈。

translations.literal: Day dinghai: he viewed lanterns at the Gate of Eastern Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he watched lanterns at the Gate of Eastern Brilliance.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，蠲秀州水災民租。

translations.literal: Day wuxu: rent was remitted for flood victims in Xiu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Xiu prefecture’s flood victims got a tax waiver.

sentences.zh: 二月庚子，大赦天下。

translations.literal: Second month, day gengzi: a great amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Second month, gengzi: the realm was amnestied.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，上尊號曰應天尊道欽明仁孝皇帝。

translations.literal: Day guimao: the honorific title Responding to Heaven, Honoring the Way, Illuminating Benevolence, and Filial Piety was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao he accepted the honorific Responding to Heaven, Honoring the Way, Illuminating Benevolence, and Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 詔蘇、湖、秀州民饑，貸以廩粟。

translations.literal: Edict: the people of Su, Hu, and Xiu prefectures who were hungry were to be loaned granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: Su, Hu, and Xiu hungry families were promised state granary loans.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，制封丁謂為晉國公，馮拯為魏國公，曹利用為韓國公。

translations.literal: Day jiachen: Ding Wei was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin; Feng Zheng as Duke of Wei; Cao Liyong as Duke of Han.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Ding Wei became Duke of Jin, Feng Zheng Duke of Wei, Cao Liyong Duke of Han.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，詔徐州振貧民。

translations.literal: Day gengxu, edict: Xuzhou was to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Xuzhou was ordered to aid the destitute.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，對宰相于寢殿。

translations.literal: Day jiayin: he faced the chief ministers in the sleeping hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he met the cabinet in his sickroom.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫增劇，禱於山川神祗。

translations.literal: His illness grew severe; he prayed to the spirits of mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: As he worsened he prayed to river and mountain gods.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝大漸，遺詔皇太子于柩前即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: he was near death; his final edict ordered the crown prince to take the throne before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, dying, he commanded the heir to ascend before his bier.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后為皇太后，權處分軍國事，淑妃為皇太妃。

translations.literal: The empress was honored as empress dowager to handle military and state affairs; the imperial concubine was made imperial consort dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The empress became regent; a favored consort became imperial consort dowager.

sentences.zh: 帝是日崩于延慶殿，年五十五，在位二十六年。

translations.literal: That day the emperor died in the Hall of Extended Celebration, aged fifty-five, having reigned twenty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: That day he died in the Hall of Extended Celebration at fifty-five, after twenty-six years on the throne.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉，葬永定陵。

translations.literal: Tenth month, day jiyou: he was buried at the Yongding Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, jiyou: he was buried at Yongding Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 己未，祔太廟。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: he was enshrined in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei his tablet entered the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 天聖二年十一月，上尊諡曰文明武定章聖元孝皇帝，廟號真宗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng, eleventh month, the temple posthumous title was honored as Civil, Martial, Settling, Sagely, Primordial, Filial Emperor, temple name Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng year two, eleventh month: his temple name became Zhenzong, “True Ancestor,” with a full posthumous string of civil and martial virtues.

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，加諡膺符稽古神功讓德文明武定章聖元孝皇帝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli the posthumous title was augmented: Receiving the Mandate, Examining Antiquity, Divine Merit, Yielding Virtue, Civil, Martial, Settling, Sagely, Primordial, Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli year seven added still more epithets—Receiving the Mandate, Examining Antiquity, Divine Merit, Yielding Virtue—to his posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：真宗英悟之主。

translations.literal: Eulogy: Zhenzong was a perceptive and enlightened ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Zhenzong was keen and clear-sighted.

sentences.zh: 其初踐位，相臣李沆慮其聰明，必多作為，數奏災異以杜其侈心，蓋有所見也。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne, chief minister Li Hang feared his intelligence would lead to many initiatives and repeatedly memorialized on disasters and omens to check his extravagant heart—he had insight into something.
translations.idiomatic: At the start Li Hang, fearing an clever emperor’s itch to act, flooded him with omen memorials to curb extravagance—Hang saw what was coming.

sentences.zh: 及澶洲既盟，封禪事作，祥瑞遝臻，天書屢降，導迎奠安，一國君臣如病狂然，籲，可怪也。

translations.literal: Once the Chanyuan treaty was sealed, feng and shan rites began, auspicious signs arrived in succession, Celestial Texts descended again and again, and the whole court guided and welcomed numinous peace—the ruler and ministers of one state acted like madmen. Alas, how strange!
translations.idiomatic: After Chanyuan came fengshan, omens in swarms, Celestial Texts raining down, and a court drunk on “numinous peace”—monarch and ministers alike looked fever-mad. Strange indeed.

sentences.zh: 他日修《遼史》，見契丹故俗而後推求宋史之微言焉。

translations.literal: Another day, when the Liao history is revised, one will see Khitan old customs and then read between the lines of Song history’s subtle words.
translations.idiomatic: Someday, reading a truer Liao history against Khitan custom, Song annals will yield their subtext.

sentences.zh: 宋自太宗幽州之敗，惡言兵矣。

translations.literal: Since Taizong’s defeat at You prefecture, Song had come to hate talk of war.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong’s disaster at Youzhou, the Song court flinched from the word “war.”

sentences.zh: 契丹其主稱天，其後稱地，一歲祭天不知其幾，獵而手接飛雁，鴇自投地，皆稱為天賜，祭告而誇耀之。

translations.literal: Among the Khitan their ruler was called Heaven, their consort Earth; they sacrificed to Heaven countless times each year; when hunting they caught flying geese by hand and bustards threw themselves to the ground—all were called Heaven’s gift, reported and boasted of in sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan called their khan Heaven and his consort Earth, sacrificed to Heaven endlessly, and boasted whenever a goose flew into the hand or a bustard fell dead—each hailed as Heaven’s gift.

sentences.zh: 意者宋之諸臣，因知契丹之習，又見其君有厭兵之意，遂進神道設教之言，欲假是以動敵人之聽聞，庶幾足以潛消其窺覦之志歟？

translations.literal: Perhaps Song ministers, knowing Khitan habit and seeing their ruler’s weariness of war, advanced teachings of the divine way intending to move the enemy’s ears and secretly dull his covetous gaze?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps Song ministers, knowing Khitan pride and the emperor’s peace-weariness, staged a cult of omens to bore Liao ears and blunt its hunger?

sentences.zh: 然不思修本以制敵，又效尤焉，計亦末矣。

translations.literal: Yet they did not think to strengthen the root to control the foe and instead imitated them—surely a poor plan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they never strengthened the state to master the foe; they copied Khitan theater instead—a feeble stratagem.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以天書殉葬山陵，嗚呼賢哉！

translations.literal: Renzong buried the Celestial Texts with him in the mountain tomb—ah, how worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Renzong buried the Celestial Texts in Zhenzong’s tomb—wise at last.
